title: Etale descent of line modules on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $\{q_i:V_i\to F\}_{i\in I}$ a jointly surjective family of etale maps with each $V_i$ a scheme. Put $R_{ij}=V_i\times_FV_j$, a scheme by representability of the diagonal, with projections $p_i,p_j$. For every $i$ let $M_i$ be an ordinary invertible $\mathcal O_{V_i}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and suppose given isomorphisms $\alpha_{ij}:p_j^*M_j\xrightarrow{\sim}p_i^*M_i$ which restrict to the identity on each diagonal and satisfy $\alpha_{ik}=\alpha_{ij}\circ\alpha_{jk}$ after pullback to $V_i\times_FV_j\times_FV_k$. Then there is a line module $M$ on $F$ with identifications $q_i^*M\simeq M_i$ inducing the specified $\alpha_{ij}$. Here restrictions to a scheme are interpreted as ordinary invertible modules via the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on its Zariski and small etale sites. Moreover, for any two line modules $M,N$ on $F$, restriction is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_F}(M,N)$ to the families of module maps $q_i^*M\to q_i^*N$ agreeing on every $R_{ij}$.

proof.text: From the scheme-test joint-surjectivity hypothesis obtain CoversTop V. Indeed, on every T the sieve of arrows whose domains map to some V_i is jointly surjective: use the specified representing pullback and its point over each x. Base change of the etale chart makes its projection etale, and the representing Yoneda map gives the site arrow. All arrows between site objects are etale by the scheme-test comparison lemma. Hence this sieve is in the generating precoverage and in the etale topology. This is the private Lean lemma atlas_coversTop.

Apply the ordinary atlas tuple realization to M_i and the transition, diagonal and cocycle fields of D. It gives N and natural linear identifications e_i inducing exactly D.transition. This step requires no covering assumption and asserts no local freeness.

source.place: Tag 04TR, compatible-tuples realization and graph isomorphisms

proof.text: For each arrow U to T in the sieve of Step 1, choose a chart lift U to V_i. Apply the ordinary-identification local-frame lemma to M_i and e_i on U. Bind these covering sieves to the covering sieve of Step 1. Grothendieck-topology covering composition makes the bound sieve cover T. An arrow in it factors through one of the chosen local-frame sieves, and the associated trivialization has precisely its domain as its restriction object. This proves IsLineModule N without changing its definition.

source.place: Tag 060X, rank-one local-freeness descent, covering composition

proof.text: For arbitrary module sheaves P,Q, forget the local maps to additive sheaf maps. Their common-test-object compatibility makes them a compatible family of sections of Mathlib presheafHom. Q.isSheaf.hom and FamilyOfElementsOnObjects.IsCompatible.existsUnique_section glue them across CoversTop V. The equivalence presheafHomSectionsEquiv gives the global additive natural map. Its scalar-linearity is checked after restriction to the covering sieve and follows from local linearity, semilinear restrictions and sheaf separatedness. Bundle it as a module map. The section equation gives every local restriction, and separatedness proves uniqueness. This is the complete private Lean proof atlas_hom_descent; invertibility of P and Q is not needed.

theorem exists_lineModule_of_etale_descent
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : AlgebraicSpace S) {I : Type u} (V : I → F.EtaleSite)
    (hjoint : ∀ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj.obj) (x : T.left),
      ∃ (i : I) (U : Over S) (p : U ⟶ T)
        (r : yoneda.obj U ⟶ yoneda.obj (V i).obj.left),
        IsPullback r (yoneda.map p) (V i).obj.hom a ∧
          ∃ y : U.left, p.left.base y = x)
    (R : I → I → Over S)
    (p₁ : ∀ i j : I, R i j ⟶ (V i).obj.left)
    (p₂ : ∀ i j : I, R i j ⟶ (V j).obj.left)
    (hR : ∀ i j : I, IsPullback (yoneda.map (p₁ i j)) (yoneda.map (p₂ i j))
      (V i).obj.hom (V j).obj.hom)
    (M : ∀ i : I, (F.etaleForget.obj (V i)).Modules)
    (hM : ∀ i : I, Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible (M i))
    (D : InvertibleAtlasDescentDatum (fun i ↦ (V i).obj.left) R p₁ p₂ M) :
    (∃ (N : F.Modules), F.IsLineModule N ∧
      ∃ (e : ∀ i : I, OrdinaryEtaleIdentification F (V i) N (M i)),
        ∀ (i j : I) (T : F.EtaleSite) (a : T ⟶ V i) (b : T ⟶ V j)
          (r : T.obj.left ⟶ R i j)
          (h₁ : r ≫ p₁ i j = a.hom.left) (h₂ : r ≫ p₂ i j = b.hom.left)
          (s : ((tensorPullback (F.etaleForget.map b)).obj (M j)).val.obj (op ⊤)),
          (e i).app T a
            (((atlasTransitionOver (M i) (M j) (p₁ i j) (p₂ i j) (D.transition i j)
              r a.hom.left b.hom.left h₁ h₂).hom.app ⊤) s) = (e j).app T b s) ∧
    (∀ (P Q : F.Modules), F.IsLineModule P → F.IsLineModule Q →
      ∀ (g : ∀ i : I, (F.etalePullback (V i)).obj P ⟶ (F.etalePullback (V i)).obj Q),
        (∀ (i j : I) (T : F.EtaleSite) (a : T ⟶ V i) (b : T ⟶ V j),
          (g i).val.app (op (Over.mk a)) = (g j).val.app (op (Over.mk b))) →
        ∃! f : P ⟶ Q, ∀ i : I, (F.etalePullback (V i)).map f = g i)
